activity.notes: Theodoric succeeded his father Thiudimir in 474 as king of the Pannonian Goths and subsequently united the major Gothic warrior groups under his leadership before the conquest of Italy. ATLAS models this c.474-493 phase separately from the existing Ostrogothic Kingdom Activity beginning in 493, because the earlier authority was a mobile Gothic warrior confederation in the Balkans rather than the territorial kingdom established in Italy. 'Ostrogothic Confederation' is an editorial catalog label for that historically attested political-military authority, not a claimed contemporary formal state name.

sources.title: Theoderic the Great and Ostrogothic Italy — Oxford Bibliographies
sources.citation_text: Hans-Ulrich Wiemer states that Theoderic returned to Pannonia in 471 and in 474 succeeded his father Thiudimir, later uniting the Pannonian and Thracian Gothic groups under his leadership.

sources.title: From Attila To Theoderic: The Ostrogoths In The Balkans — Yale Scholarship Online
sources.citation_text: Wiemer's chapter describes the genesis of the warrior confederation over which Theoderic became king and treats the Balkan Ostrogothic political formation before his Italian kingdom as a distinct historical phase.

sources.title: Theoderic the Great: King of Goths, Ruler of Romans — Yale Scholarship Online
sources.citation_text: The monograph describes Theoderic in 493 as the leader of a vast Gothic confederation who then became ruler in Italy, supporting separation of the pre-493 confederation from the later Italian Ostrogothic Kingdom.
